historical_reviews.deepseek: The broad M.2 string can match a board, drive carrier or other inventory text, while the excerpt loses record boundaries and fields. It also exposes the password and omits correctness/Web or storage-safety context.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Its classification and passive storage boundary are accepted. This review makes boot versus data M.2 topology and carrier-board versus drive identity explicit without requiring a storage backup for read-only evidence alone.
historical_reviews.related_cases: M2_BD I2C and hardware rows validate management connectivity or board function; drive SMART/inventory validates installed devices. All are distinct from the carrier-board FRU object.
historical_reviews.v3_1: ED-34 allows platform topology and identity matrices as readiness inputs; storage safety and ED-38 forbid writes, resets, log deletion and autonomous verdicts.

original_test_intent: Validate the FRU identity of each applicable M.2 carrier/board assembly, correlate it with the correct physical slot group and boot/data role, and confirm its service fields agree with the approved hardware record and BMC Web.
original_method: Map M.2 boards and their slots to stable board-level FRU records, capture complete inventory through read-only BMC access, compare required board fields separately from installed NVMe identities, confirm Web parity and prove no drive, namespace, link or boot state changed.
manual_activity: The storage/platform owner maps M.2 carrier boards and slots—including the boot-device role—to FRU/Web objects, supplies board-level truth and reviews exceptions. No drive manipulation or I/O workload is part of this row.
required_inputs: M.2 board/carrier count, location, PN/revision and attached slot map
Boot, OS, data, cache or unused role of populated M.2 slots
Per-board stable FRU device/area and BMC-Web object
Rules separating board FRU from NVMe model/serial/firmware identity
Baseline NVMe device/namespace/mount/boot/link/health map for non-disturbance
Secret-safe BMC access, retention and independent storage recovery owner
safety_requirements: Do not select a record merely because any field contains M.2
Verify the target is the carrier/board FRU, not an NVMe device or unrelated inventory string
Archive complete FRU output before exact extraction
Do not run storage writes, SMART self-tests, rescan, reset, hot-remove, format or namespace changes
Do not alter FRU/firmware/power state or clear dmesg/syslog/SEL
Protect management credentials and retain redacted raw evidence
Stop on boot-device ambiguity, NVMe/namespace/link change, duplicate board identity, malformed FRU or BMC anomaly
agent_execution_scope: Confirm source and M.2 board/slot/role topology
Capture passive NVMe and boot/mount/link health baseline
Collect complete FRU inventory using approved read-only access
Resolve exact board-level records and compare required fields
Prepare mapped Web objects for operator confirmation
Perform no storage or hardware action and no verdict
engineer_actions: Define board-level expected fields and device-identity separation
Confirm Web mapping and optional-field rules
Assess inventory or storage anomalies and issue the result

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Full `fru print` is relevant, but `grep -iA6 M.2` is too broad and incomplete: it may return a drive or other field and cannot preserve record identity, all board fields, slot mapping or Web parity. Password-in-argv is unsafe.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Retain the complete FRU inventory through approved secret-safe BMC access, select each M.2 board by stable FRU device/area plus physical slot mapping, compare the entire approved board-field set and correlate the exact Web object while collecting only passive NVMe state.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: M.2 BD, `fru list`, readability/correctness/Web criteria and 10/10-minute estimates are retained; no storage operation, board count or FRU ID is inferred.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Build a board-to-slot and boot-role map, archive complete FRU data, validate exact carrier-board records against service truth, confirm Web fields and compare pre/post passive NVMe enumeration, namespaces and link health.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds storage-aware physical provenance and exact board identity while keeping the test entirely read-only.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A generic M.2 snippet or healthy NVMe device does not prove the carrier-board FRU; conversely, a correct board FRU does not validate drive data integrity or I/O performance.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: The query itself is low impact, but misidentifying the boot M.2 board can lead to incorrect service action on the OS device, so role and slot correlation are mandatory.

project_override_considerations: If M.2 connectors are integrated into the motherboard and have no dedicated FRU, the project must identify the parent FRU or declare the row not applicable. It must not invent a board record or repurpose an NVMe serial as board-FRU evidence.
expected_evidence: M.2 board/carrier physical locations, slots and boot/data role map
Stable per-board FRU device/area and Web objects
Complete redacted raw FRU inventory and exit status
Decoded board records distinct from per-drive identities
Web parity plus before/after NVMe serial/firmware/namespace/mount/boot/link/health and BMC/SEL/OS state

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The Master fields consistently request an M.2-board FRU and Web comparison. Missing board/slot mapping and expected values are incompleteness, not an internal contradiction.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Board-level FRU comparison is a clear passive operation once the project supplies topology and field truth. Storage actions are unnecessary, so the case remains conditionally executable.

review_improvement: Makes boot/data slot provenance and carrier-board-versus-drive identity explicit, eliminates the unsafe broad M.2 filter and protects live NVMe state while preserving the intended FRU/Web test.
independent_technical_reasoning: The token M.2 can appear in a board name, a drive product string or a slot description. Therefore text matching cannot establish the FRU object. The critical engineering decision is which physical carrier and slot group—including any boot device—owns the record. Complete board-level fields can then be compared without touching storage, and passive NVMe state proves non-disturbance rather than serving as the FRU oracle.
